standard_prerequisites: Chapter notation: A with braces f denotes the restricted localization of the adic ring A at f, i.e. the completion of A_f with its adic topology

Algebra, Section algebra-section-completion-noetherian: over a Noetherian ring the completion map is flat, the completion of a finite module M is M tensor the completed ring, and modules on which f is already a unit are complete
core_obligations: A_f is Noetherian, so A to A_f to its completion is flat, and for a finite A-module M the tensor product with the completion is the completion of M_f; when f is a unit on M the module is already complete

Apply this to M = A over the prime p: the ideal p of the restricted localization is p tensor the completed localization, the displayed chain of equalities is the notation unwound through these identifications
The quotient by that ideal is A/p itself (f acts as a unit on A/p, so the module is already complete), hence a domain, so the ideal is prime
proof_roadmap: Invoke the three completion observations for the finite module A over p
Unwind the displayed ideal chain and read primeness off the domain quotient
